events.title: Erlang/OTP released as open source
events.summary: Ericsson released [Erlang]/[OTP] as [open source] on December 8, 1998 — a language built for fault-tolerant telecom switches.
events.about: [Erlang] runs many lightweight processes that talk by passing messages, and restarts failed parts automatically instead of crashing the whole system — designed for 99.999% uptime on telecom equipment. WhatsApp, RabbitMQ, and CouchDB used [Erlang] for massive concurrency. [Elixir] runs on the same runtime with a friendlier syntax.

narrative.whyChosen: [Erlang] pioneered fault-tolerant, message-passing concurrency decades before [microservices] became fashionable.
narrative.whyImportant: Open-sourcing spread [Erlang] and its runtime beyond Ericsson and enabled the [Elixir] ecosystem.
narrative.problemSolved: Phone switches needed near-perfect reliability; traditional shared-memory threading and locks could not meet uptime requirements.
